before: Let $X$ be a smooth manifold with an auxiliary smooth Riemannian metric, let $J=[a,b]$ be a compact interval, and let $\beta:J\to X$ be a smooth embedding with nonzero derivative. The normal fiber at $s$ is $N_s\beta=\{v\in T_{\beta(s)}X:g(v,\dot\beta(s))=0\}$. A **formal scalar jet along $\beta$** means a family of symmetric coordinate Taylor coefficients $T_{i,\alpha}(s)$ on a finite coordinate cover of a tubular neighborhood, smooth in $s\in J$, whose formal Taylor series transform on overlaps by the ordinary chain rule for a scalar function. Then there is an open neighborhood $U$ of $\beta(J)$ and, for either scalar field $\mathbb K=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, an $F\in C^\infty(U;\mathbb K)$ whose transverse derivatives along $\beta$ realize every prescribed coefficient $T_{i,\alpha}(s)$. The construction is uniform for a compact parameter family of such jets when all coefficient seminorms are uniformly bounded. The same assertion holds for finitely many embedded compact segments whose local formal jets are compatible on overlaps.
after: Let $X$ be a smooth manifold with an auxiliary smooth Riemannian metric, let $J=[a,b]$ be a compact interval, and let $\beta:J\to X$ be a smooth embedding with nonzero derivative. The normal fiber at $s$ is $N_s\beta=\{v\in T_{\beta(s)}X:g(v,\dot\beta(s))=0\}$. A **formal scalar jet along $\beta$** means a family of symmetric coordinate Taylor coefficients $T_{i,\alpha}(s)$ on a finite coordinate cover of a tubular neighborhood, smooth in $s\in J$, whose formal Taylor series transform on overlaps by the ordinary chain rule for a scalar function. Then there is an open neighborhood $U$ of $\beta(J)$ and, for either scalar field $\mathbb K=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, an $F\in C^\infty(U;\mathbb K)$ whose transverse derivatives along $\beta$ realize every prescribed transverse coefficient $T_{i,\alpha}(s)$. The construction is uniform for a compact parameter family of such jets when all coefficient seminorms are uniformly bounded. The same assertion holds on a finite union $A$ of embedded compact segments provided the induced full ambient jets satisfy full Whitney compatibility on that compact union: in each coordinate chart, for every $k$ and $|\alpha|\le k$, the degree-$k$ Taylor polynomials $P_x^k$ satisfy $D^\alpha P_x^k(y)-D^\alpha P_y^k(y)=o(|x-y|^{k-|\alpha|})$ uniformly for $x,y\in A$ as $|x-y|\to0$. Tangential components of a full jet are obtained by differentiating the transverse coefficients along each segment and applying the coordinate chain rule. For parameter families on the same finite union, require these Whitney remainder moduli as well as all coefficient bounds to be uniform. The single-segment construction requires no choice axiom.
